name: díchetal do chennaib
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Díchetal do chennaib was a form of divination used by the ancient Irish. Its name means composing on the fingertips. Writers are unsure how it worked. It may have been psychometry, which reads information about a person or object through touch. It may have been an incantation that used fingertips as mnemonic aids for memorizing words or syllables. It may also have been a prophecy in which bards and seers among the druids drew meaning from an automatic flood of speech. The practice rested on Celtic religious custom in Ireland. Saint Patrick permitted its continued use when he banned other divinatory arts. He allowed it because this ritual did not call on the names of the old gods.
objective: Describe the mysterious Irish ritual díchetal do chennaib and note why Saint Patrick allowed it.
key_results: The name díchetal do chennaib translates as composing on the fingertips.
Scholars are unsure whether it was psychometry or an incantation.
It may have produced prophecy through an automatic flood of speech.
Saint Patrick allowed it because it did not invoke the names of old gods.
